hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: The June 17 MOU provides a 60-day safe-passage framework but Iran re-escalated on June 20 citing Israeli violations, CENTCOM and Tehran are issuing conflicting signals about actual transit status, and analysts warn ship owners remain cautious with pre-war traffic levels far from restored, making compliance enforcement the dominant unresolved risk.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: BLS confirmed May 2026 CPI at 4.2 percent YoY, the FOMC held at 3.50 to 3.75 percent on June 17 with the dot plot revised higher to 3.6 to 4.1 percent year-end and the statement explicitly citing energy supply shocks as a driver of persistent inflation overshoot above the 2 percent target.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Hyperscaler capex is confirmed at $725 billion for 2026 with capital intensity at 45 to 57 percent of revenue, but intra-sector stock correlation has collapsed from 80 percent to 20 percent as investors punish debt-funded pure infrastructure plays and reward platforms with a demonstrated revenue-to-capex linkage, signaling the market is beginning to price ROI uncertainty rather than treating all AI capex as uniformly bullish.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold is technically trapped between the 200-day moving average near $4,340 and the 50-day moving average near $4,730 at current $4,128 spot, central bank net purchases collapsed to 16 tons in Q1 2026 versus a 225-ton-per-quarter average from 2021 to 2025, and JPMorgan notes the metal is on the back burner for most investors while Fed rate hike risks from energy-driven inflation overhang the thesis.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: Spot treatment charges confirmed at minus $70 per ton signaling extreme concentrate tightness and S&P Global projects a cumulative 3 million tonne deficit by 2036, but visible global inventories exceeded 1.3 million tonnes in March 2026, JPMorgan flags that copper prices have been volatile since the Iran conflict with macro risks not yet fully priced in, and a potential US copper tariff recommendation due by June 2026 introduces a market-fragmenting price-decoupling risk between US and ex-US benchmarks.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: AI data center power demand structural thesis remains intact with Goldman Sachs projecting a 45GW US data center power gap by 2028 and Microsoft disclosing an $80 billion backlog of Azure orders that cannot be fulfilled due to power constraints, though Sprott notes uranium spot pricing remains muted versus mining equity performance due to anemic utility contracting, creating a disconnect between the structural supply deficit and current price signals.

ALAB.note: The core AI connectivity thesis is intact with Q1 2026 revenue of $308 million up 93 percent YoY and hyperscaler capex confirmed near $400 billion combined from Google and AWS alone, but at a forward price-to-sales of 20.26x versus CRDO at 14.98x, ALAB carries a premium valuation that is increasingly difficult to justify as the market rotates away from pure infrastructure plays toward names with more diversified revenue and lower customer concentration risk.

POWL.note: The power infrastructure thesis tied to AI data center buildout remains structurally valid given Microsoft reporting an $80 billion Azure backlog constrained by power availability, but POWL at P/E 42.4 is priced for continued hyperscaler spend certainty that now faces a VIX spike to 19.49 and a market selloff driven by Big Tech weakness, creating near-term multiple compression risk even if the underlying order book holds.

MOD.note: The AI liquid cooling thesis is structurally valid as GPU density increases force thermal management upgrades across every new data center generation, but MOD is printing negative free cash flow of minus $101 million and the Consumer Cyclical sector classification makes it vulnerable to multiple compression in a stagflation regime where the Fed is signaling higher-for-longer rates, meaning the thesis is sound but the balance sheet and sector optics are a material drag.

GFS.note: GFS record backlog and 2026 design win momentum remain intact in specialty nodes for aerospace and defense, but the company is not a direct AI GPU foundry and risks being bypassed by hyperscalers accelerating custom silicon programs through TSMC and Samsung, representing clear thesis drift from a pure-play AI semiconductor beneficiary toward a niche defense-adjacent foundry story.

CRDO.note: The DustPhotonics acquisition closed in late May 2026 bringing silicon photonics PICs in-house, CRDO grew 157 percent YoY in its latest quarter, optical revenues are guided to exceed $500 million in fiscal 2027, the forward price-to-sales of 14.98x is below ALAB at 20.26x, and Zacks rates CRDO a Strong Buy versus ALAB at Hold, confirming the connectivity infrastructure thesis is intact with improving relative value.

ARM.note: ARM at P/E 118.8 remains severely overvalued as hyperscalers accelerate in-house custom silicon design using ARM architecture licenses which reduces rather than grows ARM per-chip royalty economics, and the stock is down from a prior P/E of 132.2 but still reflects no margin of safety against a capex cycle deceleration or any shift by a major licensee toward RISC-V alternatives.

S.note: SentinelOne cut 8 percent of its workforce and issued lackluster guidance, signaling operational stress that contradicts the original WATCH thesis of a turnaround candidate in AI-native cybersecurity, and at $15.13 with a P/E of 30.59 the stock has drifted from a high-growth cybersecurity compounder into a restructuring story with execution risk compounded by a VIX spike and sector rotation out of high-multiple software names.

ZS.note: Zscaler has the strongest FCF in cybersecurity at $1.1 billion but the AVOID signal reflects valuation compression risk at P/E of 26.98 as rising 10Y yields at 4.509 percent systematically reprice long-duration growth assets; FCF strength does not offset duration risk in the current macro regime.

AXON.note: AXON Q1 2026 revenue of $807 million up 34 percent with ARR at $1.5 billion confirms the public safety technology thesis is intact operationally, but at P/E 40.96 with free cash flow of only $63 million the stock is vulnerable to multiple compression in a higher-for-longer rate environment and the VIX spike today increases near-term downside risk even though the fundamental business trajectory has not changed.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.

VRT.note: Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the above 1 trillion dollar 2026 data center capex cycle with power constraint urgency confirmed by the Microsoft 80 billion dollar Azure backlog, but stretched valuation demands flawless execution at a time when macro uncertainty is high.

MU.note: MU led the chip stock rally on June 15 on Iran deal optimism and structural AI memory demand is intact given that memory cost inflation drove data center capex higher in Q1 2026, but the stock is cyclical and a stagflation-driven consumer slowdown could compress DRAM pricing outside the AI data center vertical.

AMD.note: AMD surged on June 15 following an analyst upgrade and the Iran deal catalyst, with the company announcing up to 2 billion pounds in UK AI investment and the MEXT memory optimization acquisition signaling a serious data center strategy, but the stock at 548.80 dollars trades at a premium that assumes continued hyperscaler GPU wallet share gains from Nvidia.
